findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
findings.assumptions: The value of N is derived from user input (argv[1]) and is not validated to be within a safe range before being used in memory allocation and shared memory creation.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: The program creates child processes using fork() and does not validate the input used to determine the number of processes or the matrix size.
findings.assumptions: The program does not explicitly call exec() but creates child processes that could potentially execute code based on the input size. This is a theoretical risk if the input size is used to construct command-line arguments or filenames.

findings.title: Improper Input Validation
findings.assumptions: The number of processors (MAX_PROCESSORS) is a constant, but the input size (N) is not validated to ensure it does not lead to integer division by zero or other unsafe calculations.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: The shared memory IDs (shmidA, shmidB, shmidC) are derived from user input and are used in the shmctl function without proper validation.
findings.assumptions: The shared memory IDs are not validated to ensure they are within a safe range or to prevent malicious manipulation of the shared memory segment.
